name: Huang Zezhong
profile: Huang Zezhong and his cousin Huang Yanhuang each own about 47.9% of Quanzhou Jiadeli, a Fujian maker of BOPP electrical film. That film is the core dielectric in the film capacitors used in EVs, solar and wind inverters and HVDC grid equipment. name: Yao Juhuo
profile: Yao Juhuo, a former local official known as the 'Shanxi coke king', left public employment around age 50 in the 1980s to enter the coal and coking business in Qingxu, Shanxi. deep_cut_fact: Locals still call him 'the old party secretary'; he promised fellow villagers ten years of free coal gas, and the supply has reportedly stayed free for more than 30 years, alongside family-funded projects such as Renyi New Village and Renyi Primary School in Qingxu.
current_role: Founding patriarch and shareholder of Shanxi Meijin Energy Group (Qingxu, Shanxi); no current executive role - son Yao Junliang chairs the group
research_notes: Born c.1931 (aged 65 in 1996), so now about 95; no death report found but no recent news either - treat alive as unknown. Last on rich lists in 2010. Any outreach should go via Meijin Energy (SZSE 000723) board secretary; no published email found.

deep_cut_fact: He started as an accountant: a finance/accounting graduate of Hangzhou Dianzi University (b. 1957, Zhejiang), he joined Beijing Electron Tube Factory's finance department in 1982, was sent to Hong Kong for 3 months to study international finance, and became the factory's director at just 35 in 1992.
current_role: Executive Director and Chair of the Strategy & Investment Committee, ESWIN Computing (Beijing; HKEX-listed Oct 2026); controls ESWIN group via ESWIN Technology
public_contact: ir_email: ir@eswincomputing.com | press_email: branding@eswincomputing.com | official_website: https://www.eswincomputing.com

profile: Cornell MBA Ashish Bharat Ram, of Delhi's Shriram business family, apprenticed at SRF for over five years before becoming MD in 2007 and later Chairman & MD. name: Ran Shaul
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur (Tel Aviv University) who co-founded K Health in 2016 with Allon Bloch, Israel Roth and Adam Singolda. K Health uses AI trained on millions of anonymised medical records to power a symptom checker and virtual primary care, partnering with health systems such as Cedars-Sinai; it reached unicorn status. Shaul leads product.
interesting_fact: K Health's pitch is 'a doctor in your pocket': its AI compares a user's symptoms against millions of patient records to show how doctors diagnosed similar people, before routing them to a clinician - Shaul has explained the approach on podcasts such as The MAML Podcast.
deep_cut_fact: In 2005 he co-founded Pursway, an audience-targeting startup that mapped real-life relationships among 150m+ North American consumers using machine-learning and techniques borrowed from anti-terrorism link analysis; it was acquired by Interpublic (IPG) in 2015.
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, K Health (New York / Tel Aviv)
research_notes: Has done podcast interviews before (MAML podcast) - receptive to podcast format. Route via K Health press team.

name: Augusto Marietti
profile: Rome-born entrepreneur who started Mashape with schoolmate Marco Palladino in a rented Milan garage in 2009, moved to San Francisco after failing to raise money in Italy, and pivoted to an API marketplace. Mashape became Kong, whose open-source API gateway grew into an enterprise API/AI-gateway platform; Kong reached unicorn status (~$2B valuation).
interesting_fact: He and his co-founders lived on about $1,000 a month in Silicon Valley, gave themselves '90 days to make it or break it', and got their first break after cold-emailing hundreds of contacts from a Stanford entrepreneurship event list.
deep_cut_fact: Travis Kalanick let him stay at his San Francisco 'JamPad' for a few weeks on one condition: Marietti had to cook carbonara for Kalanick's partner once a week. He told the story on the a16z podcast with Martin Casado.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Kong Inc. (API and AI connectivity platform, San Francisco)
research_notes: Goes by 'Aghi'. Open, story-friendly founder who appears on podcasts (a16z) and in Business Insider. Kong now positions itself around AI-agent/API connectivity, which fits AI infrastructure. Best route: press@konghq.com.

name: Marco Palladino
profile: Italian-born, self-taught engineer who co-founded API marketplace Mashape in Milan (2009-10) with Augusto Marietti, moved to San Francisco in 2011, and pivoted it into Kong, the open-source API gateway (2015) that became a cloud-native API and AI-connectivity platform. Kong passed $100m ARR and raised at a ~$2bn valuation in 2024; as CTO he now focuses on APIs for AI agents.
interesting_fact: Kong began in a garage in Milan: Marietti and Palladino struggled to raise money because few Italian investors understood APIs, so in 2011 they moved to San Francisco and slept on friends' couches while building Mashape.
deep_cut_fact: He has been a self-taught programmer since about age 13 and still recalls coding on Windows 3.1 on a 486 PC 'with a Turbo button' - an early fascination with networking software that led him to RPC/HTTP APIs in the SOA/Web Services era.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Kong Inc. (San Francisco)
research_notes: Active technical voice: frequent conference speaker and podcast guest (e.g. Software Engineering Daily, The Business of Open Source). Natural fit for an AI-infrastructure episode (API gateways for LLM/agent traffic). Personal social handles not verified from an official source.

deep_cut_fact: He started at Northwestern as a chemical engineering major, but robotics hooked him when he won the 2009 McCormick Autonomous Robot Design Competition with classmates Andrew Dai and Eric West. He has no published email or verified social handle; try LinkedIn or Northwestern Engineering alumni channels. Shield AI's press office is not a good route since he left.

name: Brandon Tseng
profile: Former Navy SEAL officer and surface warfare officer (7 years; deployed to Afghanistan and the Pacific) who co-founded Shield AI in 2015 with his brother Ryan Tseng and Andrew Reiter. interesting_fact: His thesis is that the AI pilot matters more than the airframe; in 2026 he said he now expects autonomous defense systems to be ubiquitous by 2040-45, not his original 2035 forecast, because procurement moved slower than he expected.

current_role: Co-founder and President, Shield AI
research_notes: Frequent podcast/op-ed guest (Masters of Scale, War on the Rocks), so receptive to media. AI/autonomy plus defense angle; adjacent rather than core to energy/data centers. Shield AI's own site blocked automated fetch; personal social handles not verified.

name: Mukul Dhankhar
profile: IIT Delhi-trained computer-vision engineer who worked on camera-based perception for Toyota before co-founding Mashgin in 2013 with his IIT dorm-mate Abhinai Srivastava (YC W15). Mashgin's kiosks recognise multiple items without barcodes in about half a second; its 2022 NEA-led Series B valued it at $1.5bn, with kiosks in stadiums, airports, convenience stores and corporate cafeterias.
interesting_fact: Mashgin's kiosks ring up multiple items in roughly half a second with ~99.9% identification accuracy and no barcodes, and are installed at venues such as Madison Square Garden, Citi Field and Arrowhead Stadium.
deep_cut_fact: The idea came from his own lunch break: while working on computer vision for Toyota in the early 2010s, he spent 30-40 minutes a day queuing in the corporate cafeteria, built a camera-based checkout demo, flew to California to pitch it, and won over his former IIT Delhi dorm-mate Abhinai.
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Mashgin (computer-vision self-checkout, Palo Alto/San Francisco)

name: Anand Babu Periasamy

name: Frederick Kautz
profile: Software engineer named among MinIO's co-founders in 2015 coverage (Nov 2014 founding, after he was a senior principal engineer at Red Hat and CTO of GridX); MinIO's own site now credits three other founders. deep_cut_fact: He defined the term 'CNF: Cloud Native Network Function', the idea of running telecom network functions on Kubernetes-style cloud infrastructure, and in 2019 built one of the first federated-learning platforms for healthcare research that kept patient data private.
current_role: Cloud-native security / zero-trust architect and open-source leader; SPIFFE Steering Committee member (current employer not confirmed; TheOrg lists HumanForm Technologies)
